questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.question_text: Consider the Boolean function F(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(0, 2, 5, 7, 8, 10, 13, 15) with don't-care conditions d(A, B, C, D) = \sum m(1, 9). What is the minimum number of essential prime implicants and literals in the minimal SOP expression?
questions.solution_explanation: Group terms into 8-cell and 4-cell subcubes. m(0,2,8,10) + d(1,9) groups with B'D' and m(5,7,13,15) groups with BD. The minimized SOP is B'D' + BD = B \odot D, which has 2 essential prime implicants with 2 literals each.

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.question_text: Consider the recurrence relation: T(n) = 3T(n/4) + n \log n with T(1) = \Theta(1). What is the asymptotic time complexity of T(n)?
questions.solution_explanation: Apply Master Theorem: a = 3, b = 4, f(n) = n \log n. Here \log_4(3) \approx 0.792. Since f(n) = \Omega(n^{\log_4 3 + \epsilon}) for \epsilon \approx 0.2 and 3(n/4 \log(n/4)) \le (3/4) n \log n (regularity holds), Case 3 applies: T(n) = \Theta(n \log n).

questions.subject: Compiler Design
questions.question_text: Consider the expression: x = a + b * c - (d / e + f). What is the minimum number of temporary variables required to generate Three-Address Code without modifying operand registers?
questions.solution_explanation: Evaluation: t1 = b * c; t2 = a + t1; t3 = d / e; t4 = t3 + f; x = t2 - t4. 4 temporary variables (t1, t2, t3, t4) are required.

Operating Systems
questions.question_text: A disk queue contains requests for cylinders: 98, 183, 37, 122, 14, 124, 65, 67. The head is currently at cylinder 53 moving toward higher cylinder numbers. Using the SCAN algorithm on a disk with 200 cylinders (0-199), what is the total head movement?
questions.solution_explanation: SCAN moves to cylinder 199 first, then reverses down: Head moves 53 -> 65 -> 67 -> 98 -> 122 -> 124 -> 183 -> 199 (movement = 199 - 53 = 146). Then reverses: 199 -> 37 -> 14 (movement = 199 - 14 = 185). Total head movement = (199 - 53) + (199 - 14) = 146 + 185 = 331 tracks (or if end is 199: 146 + 90 = 236).

questions.subject: General Aptitude
questions.question_text: If 12 men or 18 women can reap a field in 14 days, in how many days can 8 men and 16 women reap the same field working at the same rate?
questions.solution_explanation: 12 men = 18 women => 1 man = 1.5 women. 8 men + 16 women = 8 * 1.5 + 16 = 12 + 16 = 28 women. Days required = (18 women * 14 days) / 28 women = 9 days.

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.question_text: Which of the following decision problems is DECIDABLE for a Turing Machine M?

options.A: Whether M halts on the blank input string.
options.B: Whether the language accepted by M is empty (L(M) = \emptyset).
options.C: Whether M has more than 10 states.
options.D: Whether M accepts a regular language.

questions.solution_explanation: Checking whether a Turing Machine's state set has cardinality > 10 is a syntactic inspection of the TM's static finite description, which is decidable in O(1). The others are semantic properties of Turing Machine languages and are undecidable by Rice's Theorem.

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is TRUE regarding Pushdown Automata (PDA)?

options.A: Deterministic PDAs (DPDA) have the same expressive power as Non-deterministic PDAs (NPDA).
options.B: The language {w w^R | w \in {0, 1}^*} can be accepted by a DPDA.
options.C: Every context-free language can be accepted by a 2-stack DPDA.
options.D: NPDAs are strictly more powerful than DPDAs for context-free language recognition.

questions.solution_explanation: DPDAs recognize only deterministic context-free languages (DCFLs). Languages like palindromes without center marker {w w^R} require non-deterministic branching and cannot be accepted by any DPDA. Thus NPDAs are strictly more expressive.

How many tokens are identified by the lexical analyzer for the following C code fragment?
`int count = 10; float val = count + ++count;`
questions.solution_explanation: Tokens: (1) int, (2) count, (3) =, (4) 10, (5) ;, (6) float, (7) val, (8) =, (9) count, (10) +, (11) ++, (12) count, (13) ;. Total = 13 tokens (plus end marker or semicolon counting). Standard token count is 13.

options.A: {t.Name | Student(t) \land \forall c (Course(c) \land c.Dept = 'CS' \implies \exists e (Enroll(e) \land e.Sid = t.Sid \land e.Cid = c.Cid))}
options.B: {t.Name | Student(t) \land \exists c (Course(c) \land c.Dept = 'CS' \land \exists e (Enroll(e) \land e.Sid = t.Sid))}

questions.solution_explanation: Division in TRC is formulated as universal quantification: for all courses c, if c is in CS, there must exist an enrollment record e linking the student to course c. Option A is the precise formula.

questions.question_text: Which regular expression is equivalent to the language of all binary strings that do NOT contain '00' as a substring?
questions.solution_explanation: Any '0' must be preceded or followed by a '1' unless it is at the very end. (1 + 01)* ensures that every 0 is immediately preceded by the start or a 1 and followed by a 1. The suffix (0 + \epsilon) allows a trailing 0. This strictly forbids consecutive '00'.

questions.solution_explanation: When a bucket with local depth d_l splits and d_l == global depth d_g, the directory must double its size and increment its global depth by 1. Hence, new global depth = 3 + 1 = 4.

options.A: Strings where the number of a's is strictly greater than b's
options.B: Strings with an equal number of a's and b's

questions.solution_explanation: Every rule either adds one 'a' and one 'b' simultaneously (aSb or bSa) or concatenates two balanced strings (SS). The base case \epsilon has 0 a's and 0 b's. Hence it generates all strings with an equal number of a's and b's.

options.A: Only after the CPU executes a HALT instruction
options.B: For one bus cycle while the CPU is executing an internal instruction
options.C: For an entire block transfer continuously
options.D: Only when an external I/O interrupt occurs

questions.solution_explanation: In cycle stealing mode, the DMA controller requests and steals one bus cycle from the CPU (typically when the CPU is not accessing memory), transferring one word without halting CPU processing completely.

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.question_text: Consider n activities sorted by finish times: f_1 \le f_2 \le \dots \le f_n. The greedy choice selects the activity that finishes earliest. What is the overall running time to find the maximum mutually compatible activity set once sorted?
questions.solution_explanation: Since the activities are already pre-sorted by finish times, a single linear scan through the n activities comparing the start time of the next activity with the finish time of the last selected activity suffices. Thus, the scan takes O(n) time.

questions.subject: Algorithms
questions.question_text:
Let G = (V, E) be an undirected connected graph with distinct positive edge weights. Which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
S1: The shortest edge of G always belongs to every Minimum Spanning Tree.
S2: If an edge e is the heaviest edge on some cycle in G, then e cannot belong to any MST.

options.C: Both S1 and S2 are true
options.D: Neither S1 nor S2 is true

questions.solution_explanation: By the Cut Property, the edge with minimum weight across any cut (and in particular the lightest edge of the graph) must belong to the MST. By the Cycle Property, the strictly maximum weight edge in any cycle cannot belong to any MST. Since edge weights are distinct, both S1 and S2 are strictly true.

questions.subject: Theory of Computation
questions.question_text: Which of the following languages is Context-Free but NOT Regular?
questions.solution_explanation: In L = {a^n b^m c^n}, a pushdown automaton can push a's on stack, ignore b's, and pop a's for each c. Since it requires matching only two components across an intervening symbol, it is a deterministic CFL. The others are non-context-free.

questions.subject: Operating Systems
questions.question_text: An inode-based file system uses 12 direct block pointers, 1 singly-indirect, 1 doubly-indirect, and 1 triply-indirect pointer. If block size is 4 KB and disk block addresses are 4 bytes, what is the maximum file size addressable by the singly-indirect pointer?
questions.solution_explanation: Each disk block is 4 KB = 4096 bytes. With 4-byte addresses, a block can hold 4096 / 4 = 1024 pointers. Thus, a singly-indirect pointer points to 1024 data blocks = 1024 * 4 KB = 4096 KB = 4 MB.

questions.subject: Programming and Data Structures
questions.question_text: What is the maximum number of edges in a simple bipartite graph with n vertices?
questions.solution_explanation: For a bipartite graph with vertex partitions of size k and n - k, total edges = k(n - k). This quadratic is maximized when k = n/2, giving \lfloor n/2 \rfloor \cdot \lceil n/2 \rceil = \lfloor n^2 / 4 \rfloor.

questions.subject: Digital Logic
questions.question_text: How many 3-to-8 line decoders with enable inputs are required to construct a 6-to-64 line decoder without using any other gates?
questions.solution_explanation: To generate 64 outputs using 3-to-8 decoders (each providing 8 outputs), the first level requires 64 / 8 = 8 decoders. To drive the enable inputs of these 8 decoders from the upper 3 address lines, 1 additional 3-to-8 decoder is required. Total decoders = 8 + 1 = 9.

questions.subject: Computer Organization and Architecture
questions.question_text: A 4-way set associative cache memory has a total size of 32 KB with a cache line size of 64 bytes. For a 32-bit physical address, how many bits are used for the Tag field?
questions.solution_explanation: Block offset = 6 bits (64 bytes). Total cache lines = 32KB/64B = 512 lines. In a 4-way cache, number of sets = 512 / 4 = 128 = 2^7, requiring 7 index bits. Tag bits = 32 - 7 - 6 = 19 bits.

questions.solution_explanation: Value of semaphore = Initial + V_ops - P_ops = 7 + 15 - 20 = 2.

questions.subject: Engineering Mathematics
questions.question_text: A fair 6-sided die is rolled 3 times. What is the probability that the sum of the numbers obtained is at least 17?
questions.solution_explanation: Total outcomes = 6^3 = 216. Favorable outcomes for sum >= 17: Sum 18: (6,6,6) [1 way]. Sum 17: (6,6,5), (6,5,6), (5,6,6) [3 ways]. Total favorable = 1 + 3 = 4. Probability = 4 / 216 = 1 / 54.

questions.solution_explanation: PC-relative addressing specifies the target address as an offset relative to the current Program Counter (PC). Moving code in memory keeps the relative offset invariant, enabling position-independent execution.

questions.solution_explanation: When J = K = 1, the flip-flop toggles at every clock pulse, behaving as a T flip-flop and dividing the clock frequency by 2. Thus, f_out = 10 MHz / 2 = 5 MHz.

questions.solution_explanation: A loop executing fork() 3 times produces 2^3 = 8 processes in total (including parent). Therefore, exactly 8 - 1 = 7 child processes are created.
